EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours saw intense diplomatic intervention by US President Trump, who reportedly halted an imminent Israeli strike on Beirut's Dahiyeh district and announced a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah. Despite this, cross-border hostilities in southern Lebanon continued, resulting in Israeli military casualties. Concurrently, Iran declared a suspension of talks with the US, claimed a retaliatory strike on a US-linked vessel, and issued threats regarding the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, while the US reported defensive strikes on Iranian sites.

IRAN
The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) announced two of its personnel were killed today (01 June 2026) in Qom due to an ammunition explosion, which they attributed to "war with Israel and the US." The IRGC Navy claimed a retaliatory cruise missile strike on the US-Israeli linked cargo ship "MSC Sariska" in Iraqi waters, in response to an alleged US attack on the Iranian commercial vessel "Lian Star" in the Sea of Oman. The US Central Command reported conducting defensive strikes on Iranian radar and command and control sites in Goruk, Iran, and Qeshm Island over the weekend (May 30-31), following Iran's downing of a US MQ-1 drone. Quds Force Commander Esmail Qa'ani warned that continued Israeli aggression in Lebanon and Gaza, supported by the US, could lead to the activation of other fronts and "mirror" the traffic restrictions of the Strait of Hormuz in the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Iran officially halted indirect message exchanges with the US through mediators, protesting Israeli actions in Lebanon and Gaza, though US President Trump claimed talks were "continuing at a rapid pace." Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warned residents of northern Israeli settlements to evacuate if Israel bombs Beirut. Two protesters, Mehrdad Mohammadi-nia and Ashkan Maleki, arrested during January protests in Tehran, were executed. Widespread cellular and internet outages were reported across several Iranian provinces, including Fars, Bushehr, Hormozgan, Ahvaz, Kermanshah, Tabriz, Dezful, Hamedan, Qazvin, Qom, Yazd, Shiraz, Rasht, Minab, and Tehran. Reports of fighter jet sounds and explosions were noted across these regions.

ISRAEL
Two IDF soldiers were killed in separate Hezbollah drone attacks in southern Lebanon: Cpt. Dr. Ori Yosef Silvester, 30, a Givati Brigade doctor, was killed on June 1, and Staff Sgt. Adam Tzarfati, 20, of the Maglan Unit, was killed overnight (May 31-June 1). Ten other soldiers were wounded in these incidents, including two officers and a soldier seriously, and the Shaked Battalion commander lightly. Israel carried out an airstrike in Nabatieh yesterday (May 31), killing Mohammed Mousa Mteirek, a Hezbollah missile unit commander. The IDF announced the withdrawal of the 146th Division from southern Lebanon after three months, leaving two divisions (91st and 36th) operating. The IDF had warned Beirut's Dahiyeh residents to evacuate, threatening strikes if Hezbollah continued attacks, but these planned strikes were reportedly delayed after US intervention. Cross-border rocket and drone attacks from Lebanon continued, triggering sirens across northern Israel in areas such as Safed, Kiryat Shmona, Karmiel, Metula, Rosh HaNikra, Hanita, Shlomi, Ga'aton, and Yechiam, with some interceptions and no reported injuries in most cases. Politically, the Knesset approved a preliminary bill for its dissolution (106 for, 0 against), proposing elections between September 8 and October 20. A bill to split the Attorney General's role passed a first reading (65 for, 47 against). The VAT exemption bill for purchases up to $130 was rejected again (59 against, 23 for). The Supreme Court approved the appointment of Maj. Gen. Roman Gofman as the next Mossad chief, dismissing all petitions against him.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In the Gaza Strip, the IDF announced the killing of Jamal Abu Aoun, a Hamas platoon commander and doctor at Yafa Hospital in Deir al-Balah, in an Israeli strike on Saturday (May 31). Abu Aoun was accused of commanding Hamas terrorists, planning attacks, and advancing Hamas's force-building efforts in violation of the ceasefire agreement. In the West Bank, Israeli forces operated in Hebron overnight (June 1-2), raiding the home of a militant who carried out a ramming attack yesterday (June 1) at Gush Etzion Junction, which injured three Israelis. Hamas welcomed the UN blacklisting of Israel for sexual violence in conflict zones.

LEBANON
Hezbollah continued cross-border operations, launching rockets and explosive drones into northern Israel, including against Safed, Kiryat Shmona, Karmiel, Metula, Rosh HaNikra, Hanita, Shlomi, Ga'aton, and Yechiam. Two IDF soldiers, Cpt. Dr. Ori Yosef Silvester and Staff Sgt. Adam Tzarfati, were killed in southern Lebanon in separate Hezbollah drone attacks on June 1 and overnight May 31-June 1. Ten other soldiers were wounded in these incidents. Hezbollah claimed targeting an Israeli Merkava tank near Beaufort Castle with an Ababil attack drone. Israeli airstrikes targeted and killed Mohammed Mousa Mteirek, a Hezbollah missile unit commander in Nabatieh, on May 31. Israeli airstrikes were reported in Marwaniyeh and Tyre, with Press TV reporting widespread destruction at Jabal Amel Hospital, 4 civilians killed, and 20 injured in Tyre. Israeli forces also eliminated three Hezbollah operatives north of the Litani River who were preparing to launch drones and destroyed a discovered weapons depot containing rockets and FPV drones. US President Trump announced a ceasefire agreement where Israel would not attack Beirut, and Hezbollah would cease firing at Israel, stating that Israeli forces "en route to Beirut have been turned back." The Lebanese Presidency confirmed Hezbollah's agreement to a US-proposed comprehensive ceasefire for all Lebanese territory, with negotiations planned for June 2-3 in Washington. Qatar and Egypt were noted as engaging in mediation efforts. Despite the announced ceasefire, cross-border rocket and drone attacks continued from Lebanon into Israel.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Two explosions struck a cargo vessel in the Persian Gulf, approximately 40 nautical miles southeast of Iraq's Umm Qasr, causing a fire but no reported casualties. One explosion was attributed to a drone attack. The IRGC claimed responsibility for a cruise missile strike on the US-Israeli linked "MSC Sariska" in Iraqi waters, stating it was in retaliation for an alleged US attack on the Iranian vessel "Lian Star" in the Sea of Oman. A US servicemember and a British soldier were killed during a training exercise at Erbil Air Base on May 31, prompting an investigation. An Iraqi militant, Mohammed Baqir al-Saadi, accused of supporting attacks on US interests, pleaded not guilty in a US court, stating "We are at war." The Iraqi Coordination Framework affirmed the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) as an official security institution adhering to the constitution and supporting the exclusive state control of weapons.

GULF STATES
Qatar's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, held phone calls with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi, discussing regional developments, Pakistani mediation efforts between Iran and the US, and the situation in Lebanon. Qatar affirmed its full support for efforts towards a comprehensive agreement to end the crisis. Kuwait's army announced its air defense systems were activated in response to hostile missile and drone launches, likely originating from Iran, following reports of alarms and missile launches from Iran's Khuzestan province towards Kuwait. The US Central Command confirmed intercepting two ballistic missiles launched from Iran towards a US base in Kuwait this morning (June 1), with no casualties reported. The Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) announced it processed over 300 non-Iranian vessel transit requests, mostly oil tankers, since early May, noting many ships turned off transponders to avoid detection. The IRGC Navy stated it coordinated the passage of 15 ships through the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours. US President Trump indicated that NATO allies should assist the US in the Strait of Hormuz due to their reliance on oil passing through it.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US Halts Beirut Strike & Announces Ceasefire:** US President Trump intervened to prevent an Israeli strike on Beirut's Dahiyeh district, stating that Israeli forces were turned back. He subsequently announced a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hezbollah.
2.  **IDF Casualties in Lebanon:** Two IDF soldiers, Cpt. Dr. Ori Yosef Silvester (30) and Staff Sgt. Adam Tzarfati (20), were killed in separate Hezbollah drone attacks in southern Lebanon on June 1 and overnight May 31-June 1. Ten other soldiers were wounded in these incidents.
3.  **Iran Suspends US Talks & Threatens Straits:** Iran announced a halt to indirect message exchanges with the US in protest of Israeli actions in Lebanon and Gaza, threatening a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and activation of Bab al-Mandab if Israeli aggression continues.
4.  **Iran-US Direct Military Actions:** The IRGC claimed a cruise missile strike on the US-Israeli linked "MSC Sariska" in Iraqi waters as retaliation for a US attack on the Iranian "Lian Star." Concurrently, the US Central Command reported defensive strikes on Iranian radar and drone command and control sites in Goruk, Iran, and Qeshm Island (May 30-31), in response to Iran's downing of a US MQ-1 drone.
5.  **Kuwaiti Air Defense Activated:** Kuwait's army activated its air defense systems, and the US intercepted two Iranian ballistic missiles aimed at a US base in Kuwait this morning (June 1).
6.  **Knesset Dissolution Bill Advanced:** The Israeli Knesset approved a preliminary bill for its dissolution with 106 votes in favor, signaling potential early elections between September 8 and October 20.
7.  **Mossad Chief Appointment:** The Israeli Supreme Court approved the appointment of Maj. Gen. Roman Gofman as the next head of Mossad.
8.  **Widespread Iranian Outages:** Several Iranian provinces experienced simultaneous and widespread cellular and internet outages, coinciding with reports of military aircraft sounds and explosions.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high, despite the US-brokered de-escalation of a major Israeli strike on Beirut. The continued cross-border fighting in southern Lebanon, which resulted in Israeli military casualties after the announced ceasefire, underscores its fragility and the persistent nature of flashpoints. Iran's declared suspension of talks with the US, coupled with threats to close the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, represents significant rhetorical and potential operational escalation with implications for global maritime security. The reported direct military engagements between the IRGC and US forces, even if limited, highlight the active state of confrontation. Any renewed large-scale Israeli operation in Lebanon could still provoke Iran to activate other fronts or impact vital shipping lanes. The US stance of maintaining a "blockade" on Iran adds further tension.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**US:** President Trump directly intervened to halt the planned Israeli strike on Beirut's Dahiyeh district and announced a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah. He maintained that talks with Iran were continuing, despite Iran's statements, and emphasized preserving a "blockade" on Iran. US CENTCOM confirmed defensive strikes against Iranian sites and the interception of Iranian missiles targeting a US base in Kuwait. Trump also urged NATO allies to contribute to securing the Strait of Hormuz.
**Gulf States:** Qatar's Foreign Minister engaged in diplomatic discussions with his Iranian counterpart, expressing support for a comprehensive peace agreement. Kuwait activated its air defense systems in response to hostile missile and drone launches.
**EU:** EU ambassadors are slated to discuss sanctions against Israeli ministers, notably Itamar Ben Gvir, on June 5, with foreign ministers addressing the issue on June 18-19, potentially facing a veto from Czechia. France prohibited Israeli participation in the Eurosatory arms fair, drawing strong condemnation from Israel. French President Macron welcomed Trump's efforts for an Iran agreement and emphasized support for Lebanon's sovereignty and a robust ceasefire.
**Russia:** Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister indicated US failure to "defeat Iran" as a sign of Washington's defeat. Russia's UN representative criticized Israeli expansion in Lebanese territory and deemed the deteriorating situation a direct result of "unjustified American and Israeli aggression against Iran."
**UN:** The UN Security Council convened an emergency session on Lebanon, expressing deep concern and calling for a ceasefire.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions and unverified claims mark the intelligence. Firstly, the "ceasefire" declared by President Trump for Lebanon directly conflicts with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's subsequent statement threatening strikes on Beirut if Hezbollah attacks persist and confirming ongoing IDF operations in southern Lebanon. Moreover, reports from N12 and Mannie's War Room confirm continued cross-border rocket and drone attacks from Lebanon *after* Trump's announcement, suggesting a potential breakdown, partial nature, or miscommunication regarding the ceasefire. Secondly, regarding Iran-US talks, Iran's Tasnim news agency reported a suspension of indirect message exchanges, while Trump insisted talks were "continuing at a rapid pace" and denied knowledge of any suspension. This highlights a clear disparity in official narratives surrounding these critical negotiations. Thirdly, the IRGC's claim of a cruise missile strike on the "MSC Sariska" in Iraqi waters as retaliation for a US attack on the "Lian Star" needs further verification. Initial independent reports from Iraqi officials and UKMTO noted two explosions on a cargo vessel near Umm Qasr, with one attributed to a drone, but did not definitively identify the vessel as "MSC Sariska," specify a cruise missile, or confirm IRGC involvement. Lastly, Trump's assertion about Israeli forces "en route to Beirut" being turned back is not corroborated by Israeli military reports, which mentioned preparations for airstrikes on Dahiyeh, not a ground advance on Beirut, potentially indicating rhetorical exaggeration. The attribution of IRGC personnel deaths in Qom to ammunition from a "war with Israel and the US" appears to be a propagandistic framing of an internal incident.
